title: Full diagram coverage for guide chapters 7, 9, and 10
problem: The methodology site's canonical guide reaches B+ visual density only through chapter 5. Chapters 7 (Agents), 9 (Risk classification), and 10 (Failure handling) are pure prose and tables, which under-serves concepts that earlier chapters illuminate visually. The original spec (§8.7) targeted one signature diagram and one structural diagram per major chapter — roughly 13 diagrams total — but the three chapters named here ship zero, leaving a gap between the spec intent and the published guide.
solution:
Three net-new composite components are introduced — one per target chapter — built from existing primitives where possible, with no existing component modified.

Chapter 7 receives AgentMatrix (site/src/components/AgentMatrix.astro): a two-column flex or grid layout with labelled Discovery and Delivery column headers and no centre FlowArrow. This is necessary because TrackDiagram.astro hardcodes a bidirectional FlowArrow centre column that would misrepresent the static phase-membership relationship and produce visual imbalance from the 2-vs-5 agent count asymmetry. Agent names render as simple rows or cards within each column.

Chapter 9 receives DecisionGate (site/src/components/DecisionGate.astro): three zones — an inputs column of labelled StepRow-style items (touched code paths, schemas, author identity, project rules) converging on a centred decision box labelled 'Risk Classifier', then two side-by-side output boxes (Fast Lane / Full Pipeline) reached by diverging arrows. SingleTrack cannot express fan-in → decision → fan-out without injecting out-of-contract layout logic into its default slot, so a new component is the correct approach. Estimated ~50–70 lines; reuses StepIcon, Callout, and FloatingLegend where useful.

Chapter 10 receives FailureLanes (site/src/components/FailureLanes.astro): three labelled lanes in a CSS grid (grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr on desktop) — mechanical / quality / strategic — each containing a category label, a brief response-shape description, and a small escalation-destination badge. Three separate SingleTrack instances are ruled out because the categories are parallel classifications, not ordered pipeline stages, and three instances would consume three diagram slots unnecessarily. Estimated ~60–80 lines; reuses Callout and the surface/border/accent token vocabulary.

All three components collapse to stacked single-column div cards below a single shared @media (max-width: 600px) breakpoint. This value sits between the 375px mobile and 768px tablet canonical viewports, firing on all real mobile devices (320–430px) while preserving the multi-column layout at tablet and above. The fallback uses display: flex; flex-direction: column with full-width white-surface cards matching SingleTrack's aesthetic; SVG connectors are hidden or replaced with a horizontal rule at mobile width. This is the first @media breakpoint in the codebase — global.css and all existing components currently declare none.

All three chapters map to three independent peer tasks in the Plan, exercising /cloverleaf-run-plan's max_concurrent: 3 default end-to-end. All three tasks touch site/ and carry risk_class: high (full pipeline including UI Reviewer and QA). New baselines are captured per browser (chromium, webkit, firefox) at all three configured viewports (375/768/1280px). The running diagram count after all three additions is approximately 7 (ch3: 2, ch4: 1, ch5: 1, ch7: 1, ch9: 1, ch10: 1), well within the §8.7 cap of ~13.
acceptance_criteria: Chapters 7, 9, and 10 each ship at least one diagram that visually carries the chapter's central concept at chapter 3's level of polish.
site/src/components/AgentMatrix.astro exists and is rendered in site/src/content/guide/07-agents.mdx.
site/src/components/DecisionGate.astro exists and is rendered in site/src/content/guide/09-risk.mdx.
site/src/components/FailureLanes.astro exists and is rendered in site/src/content/guide/10-failure-handling.mdx.
All three new components collapse to stacked single-column cards at max-width: 600px (verified by UI Reviewer at 375px viewport).

No existing component file (TrackDiagram.astro, SingleTrack.astro, SignatureLoop.astro, StepRow.astro, StepArrow.astro, FlowArrow.astro, FloatingLegend.astro, Callout.astro, Popover.astro, StepIcon.astro) is modified.
Existing chapters 3, 4, and 5 and all other pages (/, /start, /faq) are visually unchanged, confirmed by visual-diff pass against existing chromium baselines.
npm run build in site/ succeeds with zero warnings.
Lighthouse score on /guide/ is not worse than the v1 baseline on Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO.
New visual baselines are captured for /guide/ across chromium, webkit, and firefox at the three configured viewports (375/768/1280).
Total diagram count across the guide does not exceed 13 (the §8.7 cap); count after implementation is approximately 7.
All new diagrams use only native <details> for any interactive elements; no client-side JS is introduced.
The Plan emits a task_dag with three independent peer tasks (one per chapter) so /cloverleaf-run-plan exercises max_concurrent: 3 parallelism on this real-project Discovery output.
All three tasks carry risk_class: high, confirmed before Plan finalises.
out_of_scope: Modifying any existing component; all three new components are net-new additions alongside the existing component library.
Dark theme, search, sitemap, OG image, and custom domain.
Spec edits — §8.7 already mandates B+ density; this RFC executes on it.
Amending affected-routes.json — the existing contentRoutes entry already maps site/src/content/guide/** to /guide/.
